question:
For the matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}3 & -2\\5 & 1\end{bmatrix}$:

(a) Find the cofactors of all its elements and hence obtain $\operatorname{adj}A$.

(b) Verify that $A(\operatorname{adj}A)=|A|I$.

(c) Hence, determine $A^{-1}$.
explanation:
(a)
The minors are
$$M_{11}=1,\quad M_{12}=5,\quad M_{21}=-2,\quad M_{22}=3$$
Therefore, the cofactors are
$$A_{11}=1,\quad A_{12}=-5,\quad A_{21}=2,\quad A_{22}=3$$
The cofactor matrix is
$$\begin{bmatrix}1 & -5\\2 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$
Hence,
$$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\-5 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$

(b)
First,
$$|A|=3(1)-(-2)(5)=3+10=13$$
Now,
$$A(\operatorname{adj}A)=\begin{bmatrix}3 & -2\\5 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\-5 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\begin{bmatrix}3+10 & 6-6\\5-5 & 10+3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}13 & 0\\0 & 13\end{bmatrix}=13I$$
Thus, $A(\operatorname{adj}A)=|A|I$.

(c)
Since $|A|=13\neq0$, the inverse exists and
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{|A|}\operatorname{adj}A$$
Therefore,
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{13}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\-5 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$
